name: World
description: Awareness of the outside and interaction with it: public science, the tools of the outside, the models the hub asks, and how current the hub's own research is. Its metrics move when something outside the system changes.
purpose: Bring in what is outside the system and let the AI act on it through the best available tool.
approach: Admit tools and data sources through narrow interfaces and compare each candidate on the same tasks.
out_of_scope: What the system keeps internally and which parts of the outside a particular system has declared as its own.
milestones: 1. The offline stage of metric-the-world has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 2. The staged stage of metric-the-world has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 3. The whole stage of metric-the-world has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 4. The selected arm is the one the cascade of metric-the-world chooses (rule S33).
measures_of_success: Task pass rate and cost per passing task, per hub.
inputs: A query, and whether papers are wanted.
outputs: Material from outside the system, with its sources, and the result of using an outside tool.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("the-world", "latest Rust version")` brings in what the outside says, through Tools.

name: The Self
description: Keeps the five kinds of part working as one whole: the Assembler builds them and reports the coverage, Integrity keeps the whole honest and generic and audits the run record, and Role Understanding says what each part is for. Responds to a request by running the flow through Consciousness, Body, Intelligence and World's tools; no answer is made up when a part is missing.
purpose: Keep every part working as one whole for one request.
approach: Compose Integrity, Role Understanding and the Assembler, and call the other four containers in the order the flow says: Consciousness represents the person, Body declares where the data lives, Intelligence processes the request, Body keeps the run record and Integrity audits it.
out_of_scope: How information is processed, where the system's data lives, what the outside offers and what each person wants.
milestones: 1. The whole answers a real request as one capable assistant (metric-the-self).
measures_of_success: The whole answers a real request as one capable assistant.
inputs: A request, and the person it is for.
outputs: A response to a request, with the step of every part that took part and an honest account of the steps that have no arm yet.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("the-self", "Explain what Judgment Calls decides for a person")` runs the whole flow; the same call as `hubofhubs.run("hub-of-hubs", ...)`.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: Body
description: The AI system's form and internal context. Every part here is specified to expect adaptation to a particular system, by an adapter or by a declaration of the system's data and integrations.
purpose: Let the hub apply to one particular system by declaring where its data lives, where its requests come from and which of its integrations the AI may use, and keep the run record, the configuration, the environment variables, the secrets and the stored authentication the tools need.
approach: Compose Internal Context, Intake Sources and Hands, and let a system declare what is its own: where its data lives, where its requests come from and which integrations it already depends on.
out_of_scope: Reading or writing the data (a World tool does that), finding the right context for a request, and the tools of the outside.
milestones: 1. A system declares its own sources and acts through the hub without code written for each part (metric-the-body).
measures_of_success: A system declares its own sources and acts through the hub without code written for each part.
inputs: Nothing.
outputs: What a particular system declares about its own data and integrations.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("the-body", ...)` describes the system's declared sources, intake and integrations and keeps the run record.

name: Intelligence
description: How information is processed for one request: the long view is read, the request becomes a measurable goal, the Mind plans and writes the response from what the Subconscious and the World bring, and the result is checked for goal completion and response quality.
purpose: Turn one request and what is known into a response that meets its goal.
approach: Compose Mind, Higher Mind, Subconscious and Critical Thinking in the order the flow says, with Nervous System and Judgment Calls before a risky piece and Proactivity starting standing work.
out_of_scope: Where the system's data lives, the tools of the outside, and what a person wants (the Representative carries that).
milestones: 1. One request is answered from the information that bears on it and no more (metric-the-intelligence).
measures_of_success: One request is answered from the information that bears on it and no more.
inputs: A request and the Representative it is for.
outputs: A response to one request, with the step of every part that took part.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("the-intelligence", {"request": ..., "person": ...})` processes one request with the Representative's authority.

name: Consciousness
description: The humans who interact with the system: AI Representatives act for a person, Prioritization turns the person's priorities into ESOI, Judgment Calls decide when to ask that person, and Feedback Learning applies the person's feedback to specs and metrics.
purpose: Keep the system aligned with the humans and policies it works for.
approach: Compose Representatives, Request Intake, Prioritization, Judgment Calls and Feedback Learning, on one signal contract with the Nervous System.
out_of_scope: Raising the risk signal, judging response quality against a profile, and storing what the system remembers.
milestones: 1. A representative asks a person when that person would want to be asked and acts as the person wants (metric-the-consciousness).
measures_of_success: A representative asks a person when that person would want to be asked and acts as the person wants.
inputs: A person, and their feedback when there is some.
outputs: The person's Representative, and what the system learned from that person.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("the-consciousness", ...)` returns the person's Representative and priorities.

name: AI Session Experience
description: Lets a person work with the AI while it works, on any surface: watch each step and helper as it happens, stop at once and resume, send a correction and see it taken up, approve or refuse a risky step, see which of the system's solutions the work serves, and read the result, all through one event and control contract that any harness satisfies. Its parts are the terminal, a separate frontend and the view of structure.
purpose: Let a person watch, steer, stop and resume the AI while it works, and understand and trust what it did, on any surface and with any harness.
approach: Draw typed events from the run and send typed controls back, so one contract serves every harness and every surface; show only what the run reports, mark what it does not, and keep detail one action away.
out_of_scope: How a run is answered (the front door), what a harness does to the work, a consumer's settings, screens and data model, and any screen that needs a UI library.
milestones: 1. Let a person work with the AI while it works on any surface and harness: the requirements of docs/explanation/working-with-the-ai-while-it-works.md that a scripted session can show are met on the hub's loop and on a stream session, a separate frontend gets the same facts as plain data, and the solutions being worked on can be seen and opened (authoritative metric metric-ai-session-experience, drawn from the metrics of its three parts).
knowledge: Placement against siblings: Request Intake takes in what people ask (before a run), Judgment Calls decides whether to ask (a decision, not a screen), Prioritization orders what reaches the person, Representatives carry a person's authority, and Feedback Learning edits specs from feedback; none of them draws a run for a person or takes a stop, steer or approval while it works. It was the one terminal solution widened; the owner then split the surfaces into children because the terminal, a separate frontend and the view of structure each have their own alternatives and their own metric. It stays one solution with a sub-intent because its parts share the event and control contract and need a paragraph saying how.
measures_of_success: Each child's metric: scripted sessions right on two harnesses, every event and control crossing to plain data without terminal leaks, and the right solution shown for each sub-agent with detail only on request.
inputs: The session's events (objects or dicts), the controls sent, optionally the ESOI records and the solution ids to open.
outputs: The structure view, the plain data for a frontend and the structure as terminal lines; for converse, the exit code.
effects: None itself; its children read the records and the terminal child writes to the stream it is given.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("ai-session-experience", {"events": [...]})` returns the three views of a session. The contract (events, controls, harness adapters) is hubofhubs/the_consciousness/ai_session_experience/session_events.py. Requirements and research: docs/explanation/working-with-the-ai-while-it-works.md.

name: Critical Thinking
description: Turns a request into a measurable target, and holds the result to it. ESOI Application applies proposed edits to the specs and metrics, Metric Translation turns a request into a metric with a target, Goal Completion says whether the goal was met, Response Quality judges the response against a quality profile, and, while a goal is unmet and untried read-only means remain, it keeps working within a budget before the response is sent.
purpose: Say what success means for a request and check that it was reached.
approach: Translate the request into a metric, then check the goal, keep working while it is unmet and means remain, and judge the response quality, the checks each as their own solution.
out_of_scope: Planning and writing the response (the Mind does that), carrying out the means (the tools do that), keeping a person's preferences (Representatives do that) and deciding when to ask (Judgment Calls do that).
milestones: 1. The evidence check runs on written answers with and without supporting links. 2. A second arm exists beside it. 3. The selected arm was chosen by the seat's metric.
measures_of_success: Share of unsupported links in written answers that are reported, with no supported link reported.
inputs: A request, its response, the objective and the quality profile.
outputs: A target for a request, whether its goal was met, what was done while it was not, and how good the response is.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: Pass the answer and the evidence text: critique(answer, evidence).
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: Subconscious
description: Finds and prepares information for the Mind. It reads the system's context only through Internal Context; Local File Context makes a working folder's files usable (Cards From Files builds the cards, Folder View chooses the files to show first), the Context Retriever picks the cards and file pieces a request needs within a token budget, and Intuition offers what comes to mind unasked.
purpose: Give the Mind the information a request needs and nothing from another person's scope: cards, file chunks and memory, found and prepared.
approach: Read what Internal Context returns, pick what bears on the request with the Context Retriever within the scope of the asker, and hand the Mind the cards, the pieces and what Intuition offers, with a step for each.
out_of_scope: Retaining memories (Long-Term Memory does that), storing cards and run records (Internal Context does that) and bringing in the outside (World does that).
milestones: 1. The offline stage of metric-the-subconscious has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 2. The measured stage of metric-the-subconscious has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 3. The selected arm is the one the cascade of metric-the-subconscious chooses (rule S33).
measures_of_success: Right context admitted, nothing from another scope.
inputs: A query, and optionally a folder's files and a token budget.
outputs: The cards, the file pieces and what Intuition offered for a request, with the step of each part.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("the-subconscious", "rust release")` recalls the cards; `prepare` returns what the Mind is handed.

name: Mind
description: What the planning and responding AI can see for one request and how it outputs plans, requests and communications. Context Intake takes in what the Subconscious and the World bring, the Planner breaks the request into pieces, Delegation hands each piece to the right worker only when that is necessary, and the Response Writer outputs the plan, request or communication.
purpose: Turn one request and its context into a plan and a response.
approach: Run the four parts in order, and check the Nervous System signal and Judgment Calls before a risky step.
out_of_scope: Finding the information (Subconscious and World do that), the long view across requests (Higher Mind), deciding whether the goal was met (Critical Thinking) and deciding when to ask a person (Judgment Calls).
milestones: 1. The offline stage of metric-the-mind has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 2. The staged stage of metric-the-mind has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 3. The selected arm is the one the cascade of metric-the-mind chooses (rule S33).
measures_of_success: Answer quality per dollar and per second.
parameters: A model-call seat and a tier-selection seat (built on first use, so a prompt with no tier never asks for it).
inputs: A request, its target, the Representative's authority and the guidance, when there is some.
outputs: A plan, request or communication for one request, with the step of every part of the Mind.
effects: One model call per request, which costs what the provider charges or draws on the operator's subscription.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("the-mind", {"request": ...})` plans, delegates and writes for one request.

name: Higher Mind
description: The long view across requests: Long-Term Memory retains and recalls what happened, Objectives holds the live hierarchy of intents and goals, and Guidance gives the Planner an infrequent longer-term nudge.
purpose: Keep the AI working toward what matters beyond the request in front of it.
approach: Read Objectives, Long-Term Memory and Guidance for one request and hand the result to the Planner and Critical Thinking.
out_of_scope: Finding the information a single request needs (Subconscious does that) and planning one request (the Mind does that).
milestones: 1. The long view survives from one request to the next (metric-higher-mind).
measures_of_success: The long view survives from one request to the next.
inputs: A request and the person.
outputs: What the AI remembers, what it is working toward and the nudge it should take.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("higher-mind", {"request": ...})` returns the objectives, the memory and the nudge for a request.

name: Model Plumbing
description: The one measured path every part uses to ask a model: the Model Tier Chooser picks the model for a tier and the Vendor Model Caller reaches the vendor and steps to the next provider when one fails. Its prompt standard (model_plumbing/prompt_spec.py) also holds the rules every prompt of a consumer shares: the no-em-dash rule, the American-spelling rule (English text only) and the rule for prompts that generate solutions (priority order, sub-intents only).
purpose: Give every part one measured path to a model, so cost and failover are chosen once, and spend the model calls of the goal record's budget.
approach: Choose the measured model for the tier, ask it through the vendor caller and report the text.
out_of_scope: What to ask the model (each part does that), writing the response (the Response Writer does that) and the language models themselves, which are the vendors'.
milestones: 1. Every part asks a model through one measured path (metric-model-plumbing).
measures_of_success: Every part asks a model through one measured path.
inputs: A prompt and a tier.
outputs: The model's answer to a prompt at a tier.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("model-plumbing", {"prompt": ..., "tier": "cheap"})` asks the model measured best for the tier.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: Science
description: Looks up what public research says and returns observations a reader can cite.
purpose: Bring in public science a reader can check.
approach: Search the strongest sources available and return their findings as citable observations.
out_of_scope: Searching the web in general (Web Search does that) and reading a person's own data (Internal Context declares where it is and File Reading reads it).
milestones: 1. The offline stage of metric-the-science has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 2. The staged stage of metric-the-science has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 3. The whole stage of metric-the-science has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 4. The selected arm is the one the cascade of metric-the-science chooses (rule S33).
measures_of_success: Claims supported by sources; evidence weighed.
parameters: The web-search a search arm needs, an optional API key and contact address for the scholarly service, and a timeout.
inputs: One query or a list of queries with an optional result limit and a freshness flag; or a page address with an optional focus, part and full flag.
outputs: Observations of papers, with their sources.
effects: Makes network requests to the scholarly service or the web and keeps a short cache; counts calls against a daily limit when one is set.
usage_notes: Pass a query and read the hits of the returned observation, each with a link a reader can check.
verdict_detail: openalex_semantic leads openalex (openalex 0.05 against openalex_semantic 0.3; best guess, not yet significant, two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=0.019, 12 of 40 cases disagree; one of 3 looks, alpha 0.0167); openalex_semantic leads openalex_keywords (openalex_keywords 0.075 against openalex_semantic 0.3; best guess, not yet significant, two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=0.0234, 13 of 40 cases disagree; one of 3 looks, alpha 0.0167); openalex_semantic leads openalex_keywords_model (openalex_keywords_model 0.075 against openalex_semantic 0.3; best guess, not yet significant, two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=0.0234, 11 of 40 cases disagree; one of 3 looks, alpha 0.0167); openalex_semantic is better than openalex_semantic_and_web (two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=6.2e-31, 150 of 150 cases disagree); openalex_semantic is better than web_research (two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=1.12e-25, 150 of 150 cases disagree)

name: Tools
description: What the AI can use or do outside the system, grouped by category. A category is a solution and its integrations are its implementations, and every implementation of a category does the same job. Web Search, File Reading, File Editing, Connected System Operations and Delegated Agent Sessions are the categories.
purpose: Let the AI use the best tool of each category (web search, reading files, editing files, connected systems, agent sessions) without a product wiring each one, refusing a category the Representative's authority does not allow and data outside its data scope.
approach: Choose the best integration of each category by measurement, and keep the long tail as registry entries.
out_of_scope: Which tool the system's own data uses (Internal Context declares that), judging whether a goal was met (Goal Completion does that) and the system's enduring integrations (Hands does that).
milestones: 1. The best integration of each category is chosen by measurement (metric-the-tools).
measures_of_success: The best integration of each category is chosen by measurement.
inputs: A category and a request.
outputs: The result of using a tool, by category.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("the-tools", {"category": "web-search", "request": "latest Rust version"})` uses the tool of a category, refusing one the authority does not allow.

name: Hands
description: Makes sure a system's enduring integrations, such as an enterprise system's own AI tool registry, its LLM platform and its guardrails, are appropriately accessible to the system and used by it. The language models and guardrails themselves come from World, and generic tool calling such as MCP belongs to World as well. Specified to expect adaptation to a particular system.
purpose: Make the integrations a system already depends on accessible to the AI and actually used.
approach: Read the system's declaration of its integrations, check that each is reachable by the AI, and report the ones that are declared but unused.
out_of_scope: Calling a tool (Tools does that), supplying the models and guardrails (World and Model Plumbing do that), and measuring how much code a connection needs (a metric of Tools).
milestones: 1. A declared enterprise integration is reachable by the AI and used (metric-integration-added-with-zero-code).
measures_of_success: Per-integration code changes (target 0); days from a hub listing an integration to a user connecting it; credential isolation checks all pass.
inputs: A system's declared integrations.
outputs: Which of the system's enduring integrations are accessible to the AI and which are used.
effects: Reads the declaration and run records it was handed; writes nothing and makes no call.
usage_notes: Construct with the system's declaration (`name`, `kind`, `system`, `tool`, optional `disabled`) and its run records (`used`: the names an AI run used); call `integrations(system)`.
verdict_detail: declared_and_used leads declaration_only (declaration_only 0.5 against declared_and_used 1; best guess, not yet significant, two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=0.125, 4 of 8 cases disagree)

name: Intake Sources
description: Declares where this system's requests come from (a chat, a task queue, a place where meeting action items are written) and reads the requests waiting at each, handing each over once. The hub ships the folder queue; a system declares its own adapter.
purpose: Let a system say where its requests come from and read them, without the hub being written for that system.
approach: Offer one adapter shape for a source of requests (list the sources, pull what waits at one, each handed over once) and let a system declare its own adapter; the hub ships a folder queue.
out_of_scope: Deciding who a request is from and what to do with it (Request Intake and the flow do that) and reading or writing the system's other data (Internal Context does that).
milestones: 1. Let a system say where its requests come from and read them, without the hub being written for that system. (authoritative metric metric-intake-sources).
measures_of_success: Let a system say where its requests come from and read them, without the hub being written for that system.
inputs: A source name and a limit.
outputs: The declared sources, and the requests waiting at one of them.
effects: Reads the declared source and removes each request it hands over.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("intake-sources", {"source": "", "limit": 10})` takes the waiting requests.

name: Internal Context
description: Declares where the system's data lives and which World tool reads it. The default is local files at a folder the system names, read through File Reading. A system that keeps its data elsewhere declares that instead, with its own tool, through an adapter. The Subconscious reads the system's context only through here, and the run record goes to the run store, apart from the kept cards.
purpose: Let the AI know what a particular system knows, without the hub being written for that system: the declaration of where its data lives and whether each source belongs to the system or to a person, the configuration its tools need, and the run record the flow writes.
approach: Offer one declaration for each internal source, read it through the tool the declaration names, and keep what is read as cards; keep run records in a separate run store.
out_of_scope: Reading or writing files and operations (World tools do that), retaining or recalling memories (Long-Term Memory does that), choosing the context a request needs (Subconscious does that) and proposing cards from files (Cards From Files does that).
milestones: 1. An internal source is declared once and its context reaches the AI (metric-internal-context).
measures_of_success: An internal source is declared once and its context reaches the AI.
inputs: A query.
outputs: The declared sources of the system's data, the cards that match a query, every readable item as text by id, and the run record id.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("internal-context", "rust release")` returns the matching cards; `corpus` returns everything readable.

name: Feedback Learning
description: Applies a person's feedback to the specs and metrics, not to the instructions of every task, so a correction given once is followed afterwards. It proposes quality profile changes, which ESOI Application applies as spec and metric edits.
purpose: Make what went wrong once change behaviour afterwards: propose edits to specs, metrics and the datasets that measure them, which ESOI Application applies directly unless Judgment Calls decides to ask.
approach: Record each piece of feedback against what it corrected and adjust the behaviour it concerns.
out_of_scope: Applying the edit (ESOI Application does that), deciding the profile the person prefers (Representatives own it) and the thresholds for asking (Judgment Calls owns them).
milestones: 1. A correction given once is followed afterwards (metric-feedback-learning).
measures_of_success: A correction given once is followed afterwards.
inputs: A person's feedback, or a turn reported as handled badly through structured signals.
outputs: One proposed edit (kind, target, field, value, the person it is scoped to and why) or a proposed new case for a dataset of badly handled inputs, or the reason none can be proposed.
effects: Reads and writes nothing: it returns a proposal and leaves applying it to ESOI Application.
usage_notes: Pass the person and feedback that names what it concerns (`about`), the `field` and the new value (`to`); `concerns` is `spec` (the default), `metric` or `quality_profile`.
verdict_detail: scoped_record_edit is better than kept_note (two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=3.81e-06, 19 of 19 cases disagree)

name: Judgment Calls
description: Decides, for one person, whether to ask, proceed or decline when the Nervous System raises a risk signal. The decision may go to a human, to another agent or to a delegate. It shares one signal contract with the Nervous System. It decides whether to ask; the order of the asks and how many reach the person at once are Prioritization's.
purpose: Ask a person only when that person would want to be asked, and decide how: whether the ask blocks or waits, whether it is batched, what may continue meanwhile, and whether a change to specs or a learning step needs an ask at all (by default it does not).
approach: Take a risk signal with its severity and reason, decide per person, and let feedback move the thresholds.
out_of_scope: Raising the risk signal (the Nervous System does that) and learning the person's thresholds from feedback (Feedback Learning does that) and the order and batch of the asks it decides to make (Prioritization does that).
milestones: 1. The decision matches what the person would have chosen (metric-judgment-calls).
measures_of_success: The decision matches what the person would have chosen.
inputs: A risk signal with its severity and reason, and the person.
outputs: One decision for one person: ask, proceed or decline, and who is asked.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("judgment-calls", {"signal": {"severity": "high", "reason": "a deletion"}, "person": ""})` returns ask, proceed or decline for that person.
verdict_detail: severity_policy leads ask_every_time (ask_every_time 0.944 against severity_policy 1; best guess, not yet significant, two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=0.125, 4 of 72 cases disagree)

name: Prioritization
description: The one solution that orders, for a person, the three things that compete for their attention: the work the AI is about to start unasked (tasks, standing-work triggers), the asks the AI puts to the person (questions, decisions and approvals waiting for them), and the person's own goals, which in the hub are the milestones of the solutions of their intents. It reads what the person stated or implied and the fields the items carry, gives each place a reason and the priority in the form Metric Translation and the Planner use, and turns the person's priorities into ESOI weights. ESOI is the structure in which prioritization is carried out. It works with Proactivity, Judgment Calls, Objectives, Critical Thinking, Representatives and Guidance.
purpose: Put what competes for a person's attention in the order they would: their work, the asks to them and their goals.
approach: Read the items' own fields and what the person stated or implied, and order by the rules they state and the fields carry. Three subjects share one rule set with the subject's own signals added. Work (what is due unasked): the person's rank, deadline, who is waiting, what blocks it and the time since a nudge. Asks (what is waiting for the person): what each unblocks first, then deadline, the effort to answer and when the person was last asked, with a batch limit so only that many are put in front of them at once and the held remainder says why it waits. Goals (what the person cares about) are solution milestones as the ESOI specification defines them, each a priority of one solution of an intent with a target time, dependencies on other milestones and, when the person gave one, a metric value (a milestone with none is ordered by the same fields): a met milestone or one whose end condition passed is held back, what the person said about a milestone's solution or intent counts for it, and the order follows the person's own rank, what reaching the milestone unblocks and the earlier target time. Proactivity asks it to order due work, Judgment Calls to order and batch the asks it decided to make, and Objectives which goals matter most.
out_of_scope: Whether an ask is made at all (Judgment Calls decides that), holding the goals and their progress (Objectives does that), carrying the person's preferences (Representatives do that), turning a request into a metric (Metric Translation does that), long-term nudges (Guidance does that), deciding what is due (Proactivity does that) and whether work may be done unasked (Judgment Calls does that).
milestones: 1. The weights the system derives match the priorities the person confirms (authoritative metric metric-human-prioritization).
measures_of_success: Work, asks and goals each come back in the order the person would give; the weights the system derives match the priorities the person confirms (authoritative metric metric-human-prioritization).
inputs: A person, a request, the items to order with the fields their data carries, the subject (work, asks or goals), what the person stated or implied, how many asks to put in front of them at once, and the time.
outputs: The items in order, each with its place, the reason in words and a metric-ready priority (milestone, weight, due, criterion); the items held back, by the person's constraints or beyond the batch, with why; and the quality profile weights.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: the arms are pure functions of what they are given.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("prioritization", {"person": "...", "candidates": [...], "stated": {...}, "now": "2026-07-12T09:00:00Z"})` returns the ordered work; add `"subject": "asks"` and `"batch_limit": 3` for the asks, or `"subject": "goals"` with milestone candidates (`kind` `milestone`, `solution`, `intent`, `metric`, `deadline`, `blocked_by`, `unblocks`, `met`) for the goals. In a person's words it is asked for as: what should I do first, what matters most today, put my tasks, asks and goals in order, what can wait.
verdict_detail: stated_fields is better than as_given (two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=2.33e-10, 33 of 34 cases disagree)

name: Representatives
description: The AI personas that act for a person or a team. A Representative carries the person's authority, preferences and quality profile into every request, and the sub-goals of that request carry the same authority.
purpose: Let an AI act for a person the way that person would want, within the authority the person gave: the worker categories allowed, the data scope (whose data the AI may read), the person's asking policy and quality profile.
approach: Give each representative the person's judgment about asking and the person's feedback.
out_of_scope: Deciding when to ask (Judgment Calls does that), learning from feedback (Feedback Learning does that) and translating implied priorities (Prioritization does that).
milestones: 1. A representative acts as its person would want (metric-the-representatives).
measures_of_success: A representative acts as its person would want.
inputs: A person.
outputs: The person's authority, preferences and quality profile for a request.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("the-representatives", "")` returns the person's authority, data scope and preferences. In a person's words it is asked for as: answer or write as me, in my voice or my style, on my behalf, with my authority, the way I would say it.

name: Request Intake
description: Takes in the requests people make from every source Body declares and attaches each to the person who made it, so the rest of the flow can ask for that person's Representative.
purpose: Take in every request a person makes, once, from wherever the system listens.
approach: For each source Body declares, pull the waiting requests once, attach each to the person it is from, and hand them to the flow.
out_of_scope: Where requests come from (Body's Intake Sources define the adapters), answering them (the flow does that) and what each person is allowed (Representatives do that).
milestones: 1. Take in every request a person makes, once, from wherever the system listens. (authoritative metric metric-request-intake).
measures_of_success: Take in every request a person makes, once, from wherever the system listens.
inputs: Which sources to read, and optionally one person.
outputs: A list of requests, each with its text, person and source.
effects: Reads the sources through Intake Sources and takes each request out of its source so it is handed over once.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("request-intake", {"person": ""})` returns the waiting requests.

name: Nervous System
description: Watches a run and raises at most one small risk signal, with a severity and a reason, when a step cannot be undone or belongs to a person, and leaves ordinary work alone. The signal goes to Judgment Calls.
purpose: Send one risk signal, a severity and a reason, before irreversible or person-owned steps, without slowing ordinary work and without routing.
approach: Read a short digest of each step by rule and send one risk signal: high for a step a person should authorize, medium for a step the rules cannot classify, none for plain reading.
out_of_scope: Deciding whether to ask a particular person (Judgment Calls does that), routing a run (the Planner and Delegation do that) and carrying out the step (the tools do that).
milestones: 1. The offline stage of metric-nervous-system has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 2. The measured stage of metric-nervous-system has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 3. The selected arm is the one the cascade of metric-nervous-system chooses (rule S33).
measures_of_success: Risks caught against false alarms, and latency.
parameters: The rules the consumer replaces to carry its own policy (the classes of consent and the read and consent actions).
inputs: A short digest of the run.
outputs: One risk signal: a severity (none, low, medium or high) and a reason; it never raises and never routes.
effects: None beyond the signal: the arm reads a digest by rule and makes no model call.
usage_notes: The signal goes to Judgment Calls, which decides for the person; the overseer that routed a running worker five ways is a helper of Delegation, not an arm of this seat.
verdict_detail: consent_gate leads none (none 0.65 against consent_gate 0.743; best guess, not yet significant, two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=0.718, 52 of 60 cases disagree); consent_gate leads overseer (overseer 0.917 against consent_gate 1; best guess, not yet significant, two-sided exact Fisher test on the pass counts (no per-case rows), Holm-adjusted p=0.718, overseer passed 33 of 36, consent_gate 36 of 36); consent_gate leads two_stage (two_stage 0.944 against consent_gate 1; best guess, not yet significant, two-sided exact Fisher test on the pass counts (no per-case rows), Holm-adjusted p=0.718, two_stage passed 34 of 36, consent_gate 36 of 36)

name: Proactivity
description: Says which of the system's standing schedules are due, by calendar period in their own zone, on the days of the week and at the time of day a schedule keeps (with a grace window), by a requested run or by an event since the last run, so the system acts without being asked.
purpose: Let the system start its standing work when it is due, without being asked.
approach: Given the system's standing schedules and the time, say which are due and as what request, so the Planner can plan them; each trigger says its kind (a requested run, an event, a calendar period, a window of days and time of day, or elapsed time). A schedule may carry a window (`days`, `run_time`, `time_zone`, `grace_minutes`): it is due once in each occasion, from the local time of day until the grace window ends, and not again until the next occasion. Events of a consumer's own come through Body's Intake Sources and are attached to the schedules that name their source. The due work and the other work waiting go to Prioritization, which says what matters first, and the triggers come back in that order. The arms differ in how due is decided (calendar, event, window or elapsed hours).
out_of_scope: Doing the work (the flow does that) and deciding whether it may be done unasked (Judgment Calls and the Nervous System do that).
milestones: 1. Let the system start its standing work when it is due, without being asked. (authoritative metric metric-proactivity).
measures_of_success: Let the system start its standing work when it is due, without being asked.
inputs: The schedules, the time, the events pulled from Intake Sources and, optionally, a Prioritization answer.
outputs: The triggers that are due, in priority order when Prioritization was asked: schedule, kind, reason, the request to run, and rank, priority reason and metric.
effects: Reads the schedules it is given and the time; it starts nothing itself.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("proactivity", {"schedules": [...], "now": "2026-07-12T09:00:00Z"})` returns the due triggers; docs/how-to/build-an-autopilot-on-the-hub.md builds a whole autopilot on it. In a person's words it is asked for as: do it without being asked, remind me when it is due, run it on a schedule, check back later, keep a long-running job going in the background.
verdict_detail: calendar_and_events is better than elapsed_hours (two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=9.54e-07, 21 of 43 cases disagree)

name: Assembler
description: Builds every seat from its selected arm and reports which seats are built and, for each that is not, the line that says exactly what to pass or set. It runs nothing for a request.
purpose: Build the whole from the best-measured arm of every seat and report its coverage, with no glue written by the consumer.
approach: Resolve each seat's selected arm and its needs, build what can be built and report what is still pending.
out_of_scope: Running a request (The Self does that), deciding what a part does, and judging whether a response is good.
milestones: 1. The offline stage of metric-the-assembler has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 2. The production stage of metric-the-assembler has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 3. The selected arm is the one the cascade of metric-the-assembler chooses (rule S33).
measures_of_success: End-to-end pass rate on a production consumer.
inputs: Free text.
outputs: Which seats are built, which are pending with the line that says what to pass or set, and the share built.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("the-assembler", {})` reports the coverage of the hub from the environment it is given.

name: Integrity
description: Keeps the hub generic: claims match evidence, records match code, and only failures that are hidden are reported. Audits the hub for consumer wording and how stale its research is. A documented default is never an integrity finding.
purpose: Keep the whole honest and usable by any consumer: what the system says about itself and what it did matches the record.
approach: Audit what the hub says about itself against what it holds and did: consumer wording found by scan, the steps of a run record that do not say why they did not run, and answers given with no Response Writer step.
out_of_scope: Judging whether an answer to a person is good (Response Quality does that), fixing what it finds, and choosing which arm is best.
milestones: 1. Consumer-specific strings found by the scan: none (metric-system-integrity).
measures_of_success: Consumer-specific strings found by scan (target 0).
inputs: The terms that count as consumer wording.
outputs: Consumer-specific strings found, the findings against a run record, stale areas and the share of connections that need no code.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("system-integrity", ["examplevendor"])` audits the hub for the terms given; `audit_run` audits one run record.

name: Role Understanding
description: Each part of the system knows what it is for, what it hands on and what it leaves to the others, so no part does another part's work or hides a failure of its own.
purpose: Give every part a role in the whole that the part and the Assembler can both read.
approach: State each part's role as data the part and the Assembler can read, and compare what a part does with the role it states.
out_of_scope: Building the parts, and deciding which arm of a part is best.
milestones: 1. A part's behaviour matches the role the whole gives it (metric-role-understanding).
measures_of_success: A part's behaviour matches the role the whole gives it.
inputs: The id of a part.
outputs: The role of a part (purpose, what it is not responsible for, who owns that) read from its record, and with the checking arm the contradictions the role has with the part's records and code.
effects: Reads the hub's records and the code of the part it states a role for; writes nothing and calls no other part.
usage_notes: Two arms: the recorded role, and the role checked against the part's calls; selected by the metric.
verdict_detail: checked_role leads recorded_role (recorded_role 0.785 against checked_role 1; best guess, not yet significant, two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=0.125, 4 of 13 cases disagree)

name: Learning
description: Keeps what the hub knows current with the outside by doing every knowledge search as a small systematic review: a research question and the decision it informs, a method fixed and dated before the first query, counted screening, graded items, a synthesis of what is known, contested and unknown, a decision for each candidate, what each item changed, and a date to revisit. The registry refresh is one application of it. It also reports which research areas are older than ninety days and what learning is due. An investigation is one piece of information gathering done to answer a question (a review of sources, a trial, an observation or an interview); an experiment is a research direction (its research question, owners, what is held fixed and when it is reevaluated), inside which investigations are carried out, or an investigation stands on its own. Learning carries out investigations to the ESOI standard: a question, a method fixed before searching, dated queries, counted screening, graded items, a synthesis, a decision per candidate, what was applied and a time to revisit. Every investigation is filed under at least one solution, at whatever level fits, up to the top solution when nothing narrower does (the fallback is recorded). Before a new search, Learning looks up earlier investigations of the same question for that solution and the solutions above it: a fresh one is returned as it is, a stale or smaller one is extended. Any solution can read what was already looked into before acting with `investigations_for(solution_id)`.
purpose: Keep what the hub recommends current with the outside.
approach: Take a question and the decision it informs, size the review to that decision, fix the method before searching, search through Web Search and The Science, screen, extract and grade, synthesise, decide for each candidate, state what each item changed, set the revisit date, and return the investigation record of the ESOI knowledge search standard; report what is past its revisit date.
out_of_scope: Judging whether a recommendation is still best (the metric of each solution does that), and acting on a finding (the applied part names what changes; the owner of the record changes it).
milestones: 1. Every seat's last_researched is inside the 90-day refresh window (metric-the-learning). 2. An investigation record (a review) has every part of its size, counted exclusions with reasons, grades by the rule, unknowns stated, a decision for each candidate and a revisit date (metric-the-learning, stage offline). 3. A real quick review on the subscription fast tier returns such a record (stage one).
measures_of_success: Every investigation record has the parts its size requires; every item is graded by the rule; every candidate has a decision; every finding is applied or marked not applied; research is inside its revisit date.
parameters: question, decision, weight (a size, or reversible_days, reaches, selects, dependency, outward, new_solution), links (kind:id), criteria (include_terms, exclude_terms, since, licence_allow, candidate_hosts), candidates, queries, intent_id, experiment_id, refresh_days, investigation_id, use_model.
inputs: A research question and the decision it informs for a review; an ISO date for what is stale or due.
outputs: An investigation record (investigation, items, applied, protocol, queries, screened_out, gaps), or the areas whose research is stale, or the list of what learning is due.
effects: Searches through Web Search and The Science and, with use_model, makes at most two fast tier model calls; writes nothing (investigation_store.store writes the record beside the registry).
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run('the-learning', '2026-11-03')` lists the stale areas as of that day. Through the assembled system: `system['the-learning'].review(question, decision, weight='quick')` returns the investigation record; `system['the-learning'].due_investigations('2026-11-10')` returns what learning is due, most overdue first (kind investigation, experiment or registry-area, each with the request to run); `system['the-learning'].standing_schedule(last_run)` is the weekly refresh as a schedule for Proactivity. An investigation is stored with `investigation_store.store(record)` beside the registry (files `investigations.csv` and `investigation_items.csv`; the older `research` names are still read). `python -m hubofhubs.the_world.learning.research_log research <solution_id>` lists what was researched for a solution.
verdict_detail: systematic_review is better than registry_research (two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=3.73e-09, 29 of 30 cases disagree)

name: Card Store
description: A small store that keeps cards, the hub's own memory unit, and finds them again by words or a tag.
purpose: Keep cards and find them again.
approach: Store each card under its id and search by every word of the query.
out_of_scope: Building the cards from files (Cards From Files does that) and choosing which cards a request needs (the Context Retriever does that).
milestones: 1. Every case passes: cards found again by words, nothing lost on a repeated add (metric-card-store).
measures_of_success: Cards found again by words; nothing lost on a second add of the same id.
parameters: The store location (in memory or one SQLite file).
inputs: A card to add, a card id, and a query with an optional tag and a result limit.
outputs: The id of an added card, a card or nothing for an id, the cards matching a query or a tag, whether a delete removed one, and the count.
effects: Writes and deletes cards in the store (a SQLite file when one is named); reads nothing else.
usage_notes: Default arm is local SQLite, in memory or one file. In a person's words it is asked for as: where cards are kept and found again, cards that are stale or out of date after files changed, refresh or replace what is kept, too many or duplicate cards.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: Frontend Interface
description: Gives a separate frontend, such as a web or mobile app, everything the terminal has about a session as plain data: the events and controls as JSON, and one picture of the run with its steps, helpers and their solutions, cost, files changed, messages sent and whether each was taken up, the open question and how it ended.
purpose: Let any frontend that is not a terminal draw and steer an AI session from plain data, without knowing the harness or the terminal.
approach: Carry each event and control as the data form the contract defines, fold them into one picture of the run, and keep everything specific to a terminal out of it.
out_of_scope: How a screen looks, the transport (a socket, a stream, polling), a consumer's data model and settings, drawing as text (Terminal Experience), and choosing which structure to show (Structure In View, whose result it carries).
milestones: 1. Every event and control kind crosses to plain data and back, the run facts a frontend needs are in the picture, and nothing specific to a terminal leaks (authoritative metric metric-frontend-interface).
knowledge: Placement against siblings: the contract and its adapters stay in AI Session Experience; this child is what a remote UI consumes, so it owns the plain-data form of the run (cost, helpers, changed files, steer acknowledgement, pending input), which the terminal child holds only as text. Extend before adding: it could have been a metric stage of Terminal Experience, but a frontend has different alternatives (a snapshot, a delta stream) and fails differently (a leaked escape code, a lost steer acknowledgement), so it has its own metric and arms.
measures_of_success: Share of scripted cases right: each event and control kind round-trips to a plain JSON form, each run fact is present, and no terminal-specific text appears.
inputs: Events (objects or dicts), controls, optionally a Structure In View result.
outputs: A JSON-ready picture of the run; the dict of one event or control and the object back.
effects: None: pure functions over what they are given.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("frontend-interface", {"events": [...], "controls": []})` returns the picture. A backend maps its own stream to the contract's events and sends the picture, or each event, to the page.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: Structure In View
description: Shows how ESOI is involved in what the AI is doing: the hierarchy of the solutions being worked on, which sub-agent runs on which solution, and its state and latest activity, collapsed by default; when a person opens a solution it shows the solution's fields (purpose, approach, metric and its latest value, selected implementation, milestones) and its connections (problems, ideals, delegates) with their fields.
purpose: Let a person see which solutions the AI is working on and what each sub-agent does there, on any interface, with detail only when they look for it.
approach: Arrange the session's agents by the solution each works on and read the records only for the solutions a person opens, so the overview stays small and the depth is one action away.
out_of_scope: Drawing the tree on a surface (Terminal Experience, Frontend Interface), choosing which solution a sub-agent works on (Delegation and the solution workers), editing records, and running metrics.
milestones: 1. The tree has the right hierarchy and the right solution per sub-agent, the collapsed view carries no field detail, and the expanded view carries the named fields and connections (authoritative metric metric-structure-in-view).
knowledge: Placement against siblings: Delegation hands work to workers and Solution Relevance names the solutions a request concerns, but neither shows a person the structure while the work runs; Terminal Experience and Frontend Interface draw whatever they are given, so what to show and how it nests is decided once here for every interface. Extend before adding: it could have been a step of Terminal Experience, but a frontend needs the same tree and the terminal must not own it. Source of the solution per agent: agent-started carries it (hubofhubs/the_intelligence/mind/delegation/solution_workers.py, work_solution), records come from esoi.read_tree.
measures_of_success: Share of scripted cases right: hierarchy, the solution of each sub-agent, collapsed carries no detail, expanded carries the named fields and connections, an unknown solution id is handled.
parameters: The records root (or its tables) and the solution ids to expand.
inputs: Session events and optionally the ESOI records.
outputs: Plain data: a tree of solution nodes with state, agents and latest activity, the agents with no solution, the unknown ids and the ids expanded.
effects: Reads the records; writes nothing.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("structure-in-view", {"events": [...], "records": "<records root>", "expanded": ["the-mind"]})` returns the tree; pass "*" to open every solution.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: Terminal Experience
description: Lets a person work with the AI from a plain terminal: converse with the hub line by line, or watch any harness live, with each step and helper in place, Escape to stop and keep the session, resume, a correction shown as sent and taken up, a risky step waiting for y or n, the structure of the work as lines, and the closing report. As a command (`ahohs`, `ahohs work`) it runs a goal on a real harness, or asks for one, and a follow-up continues the session; it shows the structure tree only on request, the ceilings against spend and time, the hub's own stop decision in one line, and who the AI acts for.
purpose: Let a person converse with the hub and watch, stop, resume and steer the AI from a plain terminal, with any harness.
approach: Draw the session's events and read keys and lines back as the session's controls, through one shared driver: in place with the standard library (live_session), as a full-screen Textual screen with a scrolling transcript, input history, command completion and a rendered answer (textual_session), or as plain lines (line_repl). Built on the strongest open-source parts, and the decision for every reviewed terminal (arm, part or not adopted with its reason) is recorded in the registry.
out_of_scope: The contract of events and controls and the harness adapters (AI Session Experience), plain data for a separate frontend (Frontend Interface), choosing which structure to show and what is inside it (Structure In View), how a run is answered (the front door), and a consumer's own commands, data and words, which stay in its binding (`commands`, `segments`, `panels`, `front_door`, `represent`, `records`).
milestones: 1. The requirements of docs/explanation/working-with-the-ai-while-it-works.md that a scripted session can show are met on the hub's loop and on a stream session (authoritative metric metric-terminal-session).
knowledge: Placement against siblings: the other two children draw the same events for something that is not a terminal (Frontend Interface) or decide what structure is worth showing (Structure In View); the terminal is the reference surface, so it keeps the existing code and the existing scripted metric, and its arms compete on keys, redraw and the line REPL baseline. Compared with Claude Code, Codex CLI, opencode, Aider and others on 2026-11-10 (registry area terminal_agent_experience). Adoption decisions per finding: registry area terminal_agent_experience, columns adoption, adopted_as and adoption_reason (licences read at the source on 2026-11-10); the Textual arm is built on the Textual and Rich libraries (MIT), with the consumer's own Textual screen as its starting point. Selection: live_session and textual_session tie on every scripted and real-terminal case, so the incumbent stays (esoi select --promote finds no clear winner).
measures_of_success: Share of scripted sessions right: every typed line reaches the front door, stop then resume loses nothing, a steer is taken up in the next call and shown, helpers show with their parent, a risky step waits, the same script passes on two harnesses.
inputs: A harness (start and control), a goal, a text stream, optional key source; or lines and a front door for converse.
outputs: The text written, and a SessionReport (last Finished, every run, all events, the controls and whether each was taken); for the structure, plain lines.
effects: Runs the harness in a thread, reads keys (Escape, Ctrl-C, lines), writes to the stream it is given, and redraws in place only on a terminal.
usage_notes: Contract: hubofhubs/the_consciousness/ai_session_experience/session_events.py. The command: hubofhubs/the_consciousness/ai_session_experience/terminal_experience/work.py (`ahohs work`, bare `ahohs`). Demo with no model: python -m hubofhubs.the_consciousness.ai_session_experience.terminal_experience.live --demo loop. Requirements and research: docs/explanation/working-with-the-ai-while-it-works.md.
verdict_detail: live_session is better than line_repl (two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=2.98e-08, 27 of 67 cases disagree); textual_session is exactly equal to live_session on the metric (textual_session 1 against live_session 1), so live_session stays

name: Decision Check
description: Checks a draft decision (a pick among options, or a reply) by small independent checks, each a short structured call that sees only the slice of evidence it needs, so that a cheap model gives a reliable decision through structure. When the views agree the draft is accepted at no extra cost; when they disagree one call sees only the disagreeing views and must quote the deciding evidence, or the check abstains. A failing part of a reply is rewritten or removed alone. The checks that failed before become known-mistake lines that the check's prompt carries, adopted only while the check's metric says they pay.
purpose: Give a draft decision to small independent checks that check each other's work, within a declared number of calls.
approach: Run the checks in parallel, accept where they agree, decide a disagreement from quoted evidence or abstain, repair only the failing part, and learn the mistakes found.
out_of_scope: Judging a reply against a person's quality profile (Response Quality does that), whether the goal was met (Goal Completion does that), producing the draft, and the consumer's evidence, prompts and records of mistakes (the consumer supplies them).
milestones: 1. On the labelled cases the agreement check makes no more wrong decisions than the draft as given, within its call cap (authoritative metric metric-decision-check). 2. A known-mistake line is adopted only when this metric rises on held-out cases.
measures_of_success: The share of decisions right, the wrong decisions, the model calls per decision and the share of decisions the views agreed on.
parameters: binding (kind, options, views, votes, known, max_calls, parallel); optionally the model call to use.
inputs: A draft (an option id or a reply text) and a CheckBinding the consumer fills: the options, and for each view an instruction and the evidence slice it alone sees.
outputs: The outcome, the pick or the repaired text, the calls used against the cap, the agreement and the reason, with every view and finding.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself; each model-calling arm makes its calls through Model Plumbing at the cheap tier, or through the call the caller hands in.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("decision-check", {"draft": ..., "binding": {...}})`. The learning loop (`Mistake`, `MistakeLog`, `distill`, `LineBook`, `adopt`, `retire`) is imported from hubofhubs.api and run offline by the consumer on its own records; its lines go back in through `binding.known`.
verdict_detail: agreement_check is better than draft_as_given (two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=0.00391, 10 of 21 cases disagree); single_verify is exactly equal to agreement_check on the metric (single_verify 0.952 against agreement_check 0.952), so agreement_check stays

name: ESOI Application
description: Applies a proposed change to the specs and metrics of the system, as an edit to one field of one record and never as a longer prompt, so what a request needs becomes a measured specification.
purpose: Apply a proposed edit to the system's own specs and metrics exactly as proposed: an AI is the author of the specs, and the edit is applied directly unless Judgment Calls decides to ask.
approach: Take a proposed change, find the record and field it names, set the new value and say what changed, or refuse the change with the reason and leave every record as it was.
out_of_scope: Choosing the metric for a request (Metric Translation does that), proposing edits from feedback (Feedback Learning does that) and deciding whether anyone is asked first (Judgment Calls does that).
milestones: 1. A proposed edit changes exactly the field it names, and an edit that cannot be applied is refused and changes nothing (metric-esoi-application).
measures_of_success: A proposed edit changes exactly the field it names, and a refused one changes nothing.
inputs: A proposed change to a spec, a metric, a quality profile or another ESOI record, and optionally the subject whose records it concerns.
outputs: What changed (table, target, field, before and after, or the record created or already there), that it is proposed and waiting for approval, or why the change was refused.
effects: Edits the records at the records location it was given (a RecordsSource: tables in memory by default, the rows of a service for a consumer that keeps them there); writing in-memory tables back to files is the caller's.
usage_notes: Construct with the records as `{table: {id: row}}` (problems, ideals, solutions, implementations, metrics, profiles), or with a `source` (a RecordsSource: `read(subject)` and `apply(edit)`) that says where the consumer's records live; call `apply` with a change from Feedback Learning or an `edit` of the same shape: a field edit (`spec_edit`, `metric_edit`, `problem_edit`, `ideal_edit`, `implementation_edit`, `quality_profile_edit`), or an ensure-one addition (`record_add` with a table, a key and fields; `milestone_add` with a solution, the milestone sentence and its metric). A result is applied, proposed (held for approval, not done) or refused with the reason.
verdict_detail: record_field_edit is better than append_to_description (two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=0.00195, 10 of 10 cases disagree)

name: Goal Completion
description: Says whether the goal condition of a request or sub-goal was met, against the done-standard its metric names, and whether iteration the person did not ask for should go on. It is a machine learning task, and it is not the judgment of how good the response is.
purpose: Check that the goal was met, and that unasked iteration stops when it should.
approach: Compare the outcome of a goal with its done-standard, reading the outcome's own structured facts (its coverage, its errors, its refusals) before any prose, and say met or not with a reason; given the history of the iterations so far, say continue, stop (met), stop (good enough, with what is left), stop (not worth it) or ask, so that the hub iterates only while the expected gain toward the next milestone is worth its cost and always within what the person stated and the policy that bounds it.
out_of_scope: Judging how good the response is (Response Quality does that) and making the change (the tools do that).
milestones:
1. The verdict on whether a goal was met matches the verdict of a reviewer (authoritative metric metric-goal-completion).
2. The decision on whether to iterate again matches the right decision of scripted histories, with over-iteration, premature stopping and wrong asks each scored (authoritative metric metric-goal-completion).
measures_of_success: The verdict on whether a goal was met matches the verdict of a reviewer, and the stop decision on an iteration history matches the right one.
inputs: A goal, its done-standard and the outcome; for a stop decision an iteration history (the verdict, changes, metric value, spend and time of each iteration, the ceilings, the next milestone, what the person stated, the policy and authority that bound it, and whether what is missing needs a person).
outputs: Whether the goal was met, with the reason; for an iteration history, the decision (continue, stop_met, stop_good_enough, stop_not_worth_it, ask) with its reason, the facts used and what is left.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("goal-completion", {"goal": ..., "done_standard": ..., "outcome": ...})` returns met and the reason; a worker that failed or was refused is never met. `decide_stop` takes the history and is reached through the Critical Thinking composition (`decide_stop`) or, by the delegation code, through the selected arm resolved by name; the person's stated limits, the policy and the authority are plain inputs resolved from Consciousness (`resolve_stop_limits`), and a person can always stop. Only hub-initiated iteration is judged: a person's own session runs until a ceiling they can raise.
verdict_detail: independent_review is better than evidence_standard (two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=2.33e-10, 34 of 65 cases disagree); independent_review is better than nonempty (two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=8.73e-11, 36 of 65 cases disagree); independent_review leads pragmatic_stop (pragmatic_stop 0.979 against independent_review 1; best guess, not yet significant, two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=0.5, 2 of 65 cases disagree)

name: Metric Translation
description: Turns a request into a metric with a target value or an improvement, adjustable in real time, and applies the same step recursively to each sub-goal, rolling each up to its parent objective.
purpose: Make what success means for a request explicit and measurable as a goal record: the metric, its target, the done-standard and the budget (attempts, pieces and model calls) that Delegation and Model Plumbing enforce.
approach: Turn a request into a metric with a target value or improvement and a budget on the goal record, and roll the target of a sub-goal up to its parent objective, adjustable while the work runs.
out_of_scope: Creating the specs (ESOI Application does that), keeping the objectives (Objectives does that) and checking the result (Goal Completion does that).
milestones: 1. A request is turned into a metric with a target value or improvement that a reviewer accepts (authoritative metric metric-metric-translation).
measures_of_success: A request is turned into a metric with a target value or improvement that a reviewer accepts.
inputs: A request, and the parent target when there is one.
outputs: A metric with a target value or improvement for a request or a sub-goal.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("metric-translation", {"request": ...})` returns the target, its done-standard and its budget.

name: Metric Upkeep
description: Keeps a milestone's metrics able to show progress: decides by code from each metric record's fields whether it is fresh, stale, unmeasured or without a source, reads what it can read, and adds one intermediate metric the AI can move when the milestone's own metric moves only through a person.
purpose: Keep every milestone measurable by the AI's own work, so a turn asked to make progress never has the excuse of waiting on a person.
approach: Decide each metric's state from its record fields, read a stale or unmeasured metric through the reader its source names, and add one intermediate child metric, checked by independent views to track the parent's done test, when the parent moves only through a person.
out_of_scope: Choosing a request's metric (Metric Translation does that), writing the records (ESOI Application does that), checking a decision (Decision Check does that) and doing the work the metric counts (the consumer's work step does that).
milestones: 1. A metric's state is decided from its fields alone and an intermediate metric is added once, only after the check agrees it tracks the parent (metric-metric-upkeep).
measures_of_success: States match the record fields, a reading is recorded once, and an intermediate metric is added once and only when the check agrees.
inputs: The milestone (solution id, name, done-when, moved_by), its metric records, readers by source name, today's date and a model call.
outputs: One action per metric of the milestone: its state, the action taken (none, read, propose_source, define_intermediate), and the reading, the child metric or why not.
effects: Writes a reading or one child metric record through ESOI Application at the records location the consumer gave it.
usage_notes: Construct with the ESOI Application and Decision Check seats; call `upkeep(spec, metrics, readers, today, ask)`. A metric with no readable source gets a checked proposal for how it becomes readable, kept as knowledge on the milestone's record. Justification against siblings: Metric Translation turns a request into a target, ESOI Application edits records, Goal Completion judges a goal met; none keeps the metrics themselves measurable over time.

name: Response Quality
description: Judges a response against a quality profile: a named set of criteria with weights and target values. The profile is resolved for each request from the Representative, Guidance and Prioritization, and falls back to a default profile. Each arm judges one criterion and can also repair: links held to the evidence, figures held to the evidence, no em dash, and day counts that match the calendar.
purpose: Judge a response against the quality profile that applies to this request.
approach: Resolve the profile, judge each criterion, and report one balanced score per profile.
out_of_scope: A person's own profile (Representatives own that), context-specific criteria (Guidance owns those), translating implied priorities into weights (Prioritization owns that), updating a profile from feedback (Feedback Learning owns that) and whether the goal was met (Goal Completion).
milestones: 1. One balanced score for each quality profile, with the weights and targets of the profile fixed before any method is scored (authoritative metric metric-response-quality).
measures_of_success: One balanced score for each quality profile, with the weights and targets of the profile fixed before any method is scored.
inputs: A response, the evidence behind it and the resolved quality profile (the default profile when none is given).
outputs: The findings against each criterion of the profile; an empty list means the response held.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: Each arm judges one criterion; the other criteria of the default profile have no arm yet. A consumer that wants a repair rather than a verdict imports the arm's functions by name from hubofhubs.api (remove_em_dashes, strip_unsupported, evidence_of, day_count_errors, relativize).
verdict_detail: date_arithmetic is exactly equal to evidence_check on the metric (date_arithmetic 1 against evidence_check 1), so evidence_check stays; em_dash_free is exactly equal to evidence_check on the metric (em_dash_free 1 against evidence_check 1), so evidence_check stays; grounded_figures is exactly equal to evidence_check on the metric (grounded_figures 1 against evidence_check 1), so evidence_check stays

name: Solution Passes
description: Gives each solution a request concerns its own pass of a cheap model, reading that solution's prompt formed from its own records, then narrower passes for each scope above and each dependent.
purpose: Make every relevant solution judge a request against its own records, at every level of the hierarchy, so durable memory and expertise are never skipped.
approach: Run one pass per relevant solution in parallel on its generated prompt, climb the scopes above one level at a time until a scope finds no effect on how its children combine, ask each dependent whether what it relies on still holds, and cap depth and calls without ever cutting a relevant solution's own pass.
out_of_scope: Choosing which solutions are relevant and forming their prompts (Relevant Solutions and the Subconscious do that), turning findings into the goal's target (Metric Translation does that), checking the work (Goal Completion does that) and writing records (ESOI Application does that).
milestones: 1. On the flow cases, the record that decides each case reaches the pass of a considered solution (free stage) and the cheap pass cites it and reaches the right verdict (one real case, then all) (metric-solution-passes).
measures_of_success: Each case's deciding record reaches the right pass, and the pass's verdict follows it.
parameters: tier (default cheap); limits: depth (default 3), calls (default 40), width (parallel calls, default 8).
inputs: The request, the briefs the Subconscious prepared (solutions, ancestors, dependents, each with its prompt), optional own passes by solution id, and an optional one-argument model call.
outputs: Findings per relevant solution (needs, target from its own metric, risks, conflicts with recorded results, knowledge, candidates), parent findings per level, dependent findings, calls made, passes cut and where the climb stopped.
effects: Model calls through Model Plumbing at the cheap tier.
usage_notes: Called by Critical Thinking's consider step. Justification against siblings: Decision Check tests one draft decision with independent views, Metric Translation turns a request into a target and Goal Completion judges an outcome; none gives each solution of the records its own pass on a request before the work. Working on one solution after the passes uses the same folder: build_out deepens one unit against its requirements, choose_approach proposes distinct ways from several cheap views and picks one unlabelled by the requirements, solution_frame labels what a worker needs from the solution (approach, next milestone not met, what the metric cannot see, the weakness of the way in use, the last value), and unmet_by_unit with keep_better carry what failed into the next run and keep a rewrite only when it meets more.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: Guidance
description: An infrequent, longer-term nudge to the Planner, drawn from the objectives, and the context-specific criteria for what a good response is in this situation.
purpose: Keep the Planner pointed at the longer-term outcome without taking over the request.
approach: Decide first whether this is a moment for the answer alone (urgent, upset, asked to stop, unrelated to the objectives, raised lately); otherwise name the next target of the focused or most related objective with where it stands now, in one sentence made only of what the objective holds, and carry the quality criteria the objective states.
out_of_scope: Planning (the Planner does that), a person's own preferences (the Representative carries those) and translating implied priorities (Prioritization does that).
milestones: 1. A nudge is infrequent and moves the Planner toward the longer-term outcome (authoritative metric metric-planner-guidance).
measures_of_success: A nudge is infrequent and moves the Planner toward the longer-term outcome.
inputs: A request and the objectives (id, name, next target, reading, in focus, raised lately, criteria).
outputs: `None` when no nudge is due, else the nudge sentence, the objective it points at and the quality criteria that belong to it.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("guidance", {"request": ..., "objectives": [...]})` returns the nudge or nothing; Higher Mind calls it after Objectives. Consumer-specific wording of a nudge stays in the consumer as its own arm.
