verdict_detail: rule_gate is better than always_nudge (two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=1.53e-05, 18 of 24 cases disagree); rule_gate is better than overlap_only (two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=0.000122, 14 of 24 cases disagree)

name: Long-Term Memory
description: The retention policy and the recall over the Body's store: what the system keeps across requests, for how long, and how it is found again.
purpose: Let the AI keep and recall what happened across requests.
approach: Keep dated records of what happened and recall them by relevance and recency.
out_of_scope: Where the data is stored (Internal Context declares that) and finding information for one request (Subconscious does that).
milestones: 1. A later request can use what an earlier one learned (metric-long-term-memory).
measures_of_success: A later request can use what an earlier one learned.
inputs: A query, the person, optionally the clock; or an item to retain for the person.
outputs: The person's retained items that bear on the request (id, text, at), most relevant first, newer first on a tie.
effects: Retains items in a file per person or in the Card Store, and drops what is older than the retention period; recall reads only.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("long-term-memory", {"query": "rust release", "person": ""})` recalls; the consumer calls `retain` after a request with what is worth keeping. In a person's words it is asked for as: remind me what we decided or said before, what happened last time, recall an earlier conversation or note; and it is what a graph or memory product that keeps knowledge across sessions competes to be.
verdict_detail: file_recall leads card_store_recall (card_store_recall 0.918 against file_recall 0.959; best guess, not yet significant, two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=1, 1 of 17 cases disagree); file_recall leads recent_window (recent_window 0.712 against file_recall 0.959; best guess, not yet significant, two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=0.141, 8 of 17 cases disagree)

name: Objectives
description: The live hierarchy of intents and goals across requests. A new request is placed under the objective it serves, and a goal rolls up to its parent. Which milestones matter most to the person is asked of Prioritization.
purpose: Let the AI keep working toward a goal over many requests and know which objective a request serves.
approach: Read each objective's done-standard (its criteria), roll progress up from goals to their parents, and place a request under the live objective whose own words it shares most.
out_of_scope: Turning a request into a metric (Metric Translation does that) nudging the Planner (Guidance does that) and deciding which milestones matter most to the person (Prioritization does that).
milestones: 1. An objective persists and progress is checked against its done-standard (metric-live-objectives).
measures_of_success: An objective persists and progress is checked against its done-standard.
inputs: A person and the objectives their system recorded (each with an id, a title, a parent, the criteria that say it is done and whether each is met); for a placement, also the request.
outputs: The hierarchy in order, each objective with its depth, state (not started, in progress or met) and progress rolled up from its criteria and children; or, for a request, the live objective it serves with its path from the top, or none.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: the arms are pure functions of the objectives they are given, and the system keeps the store.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("live-objectives", {"objectives": [...]})` returns the hierarchy with each objective's state and progress; the `place` call puts a request under the objective it serves. In a person's words it is asked for as: keep track of my goals and milestones over weeks, work that runs for days and must survive restarts, where a long-running goal stands; durable job and workflow engines compete here.
verdict_detail: rolled_up is better than flat_list (two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=0.000488, 12 of 20 cases disagree)

name: Context Intake
description: The one intake of the Mind. It takes what the Subconscious prepared from the system's internal context, what the World brought in and the instructions that apply to the request, and gives the Planner one view. Instructions are the third source: chosen for the request within a token budget so a task does not pay for rules it does not need, and counted in what the request costs.
purpose: Give the Planner one view of what is known for a request, whatever its source.
approach: Merge what was prepared, what the world brought and the instructions chosen for the request within a token budget into one labelled view, each line naming where it came from; picking information stays with the Subconscious.
out_of_scope: Finding or preparing the information, which is the Subconscious and the World.
milestones: 1. The Planner receives one view whatever the source of the information (authoritative metric metric-context-intake).
measures_of_success: The Planner receives one view whatever the source of the information.
inputs: A request, what the Subconscious prepared and what the World brought.
outputs: One view of the information for a request, its sources, and which instructions went in and how many tokens they cost.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("context-intake", {"request": ...})` returns the view; pass `instructions` (rules, a situation and a token budget) to add the third source.

name: Delegation
description: Hands each piece of work to the right worker, only when that is necessary. Every handoff carries the Representative's authority and a sub-goal with its own done-standard.
purpose: Hand work on without losing the authority it was given or the standard that says it is done, enforce the authority, the goal record's budget and cancellation (down to a running agent session), and refuse a piece it may not run with the reason.
approach: Hand each piece to the worker its category names only when a worker is needed, carrying the Representative's authority and the sub-goal's done-standard, enforce authority, budget and cancellation, and answer a piece that needs no worker from the view.
out_of_scope: Deciding the pieces (the Planner does that), checking the done-standard (Goal Completion does that), and carrying out the work (the tools do that).
milestones: 1. Each handoff names the authority it carries and a done-standard, and work is handed on only when necessary (authoritative metric metric-work-delegation).
measures_of_success: Each handoff names the authority it carries and a done-standard, and work is handed on only when necessary.
inputs: A piece, the Representative's authority and the sub-goal done-standard.
outputs: The result of a piece, from the worker that did it.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("delegation", {"pieces": [], "authority": {}})` returns one result per piece. `hubofhubs.the_intelligence.mind.delegation.solution_workers.work_solution(solution_id, frame=, children=, work=, check=)` works a task through the hierarchy of solutions instead of ad hoc sub-agents: one injected worker per solution, briefed only with that solution's frame and the line its parent hands down, children first (in parallel, within a shared depth, width, calls and rounds budget), their compact reports then going to the parent, each solution's next unmet milestone checked by something other than the worker; it returns a SolutionReport tree.

name: Planner
description: Breaks a request into pieces, each with the sub-goal it must meet and the worker category that fits it; on a replan it plans again only what failed. The arms are a rule router that reads the words of the request, a single-piece baseline and a model planner.
purpose: Turn a request into pieces that can be done and checked, each with the worker category that fits it, and replan from what failed.
approach: Break the request into pieces, each with the sub-goal it must meet and one worker category, and plan again only the pieces that failed when the goal was unmet; the arms differ in how they read the request (by its words, or by a model), not in what they return.
out_of_scope: Doing a piece (Delegation hands it on), and setting the target of the request (Metric Translation).
milestones: 1. Each piece of a request has a sub-goal that can be done and checked (authoritative metric metric-request-planner).
measures_of_success: Each piece of a request has a sub-goal that can be done and checked.
inputs: A request, its context, its target and the guidance, when there is some.
outputs: The pieces of a request, each with the sub-goal it must meet.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("planner", {"request": ...})` returns the pieces.
verdict_detail: cue_router is better than one_piece (two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=3.38e-08, 63 of 105 cases disagree)

name: Resolve a Reference
description: Says which one of a list of candidates a phrase refers to (a person for an owner's name, a goal for a draft's title, a post for a version of it), or abstains. The arms are an id and exact match, a model that judges sameness, and the shared-word match as the bound.
purpose: Tie a phrase to the thing it names only when it is that thing.
approach: Offer the phrase and the candidates to an arm that returns match with the one candidate's id, or abstain; a match is always a candidate offered, and the caller does nothing on an abstain except say it did not find the thing.
out_of_scope: Deciding whether the matched thing may be changed (the caller's own safety rule decides that) and finding the candidates (the caller supplies them).
milestones: 1. No look-alike is matched and the right candidates are found on the labelled set (authoritative metric metric-resolve-a-reference).
measures_of_success: The share of cases settled correctly, and the number of wrong matches.
inputs: A phrase and the candidates (id, name, optional aliases and text); optionally the model call to use.
outputs: The outcome (match or abstain), the candidate's id and a reason.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself; the model-judged arm makes one model call through Model Plumbing, or through the call the caller hands in.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("resolve-a-reference", {"phrase": ..., "candidates": [...]})`. A near-miss is an abstain, never the closest candidate. In a person's words it is asked for as: which one does it mean, what does this or that or the report refer to, who is meant by them, the thing we talked about.
verdict_detail: exact_match is better than shared_words (two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=0.0215, 10 of 32 cases disagree)

name: Route a Request
description: Decides once what a request asks of the system: to be told something (information), to have something done or changed (act), to have text written and handed back in the reply (draft), or that it cannot be acted on yet (clarify). The arms are one cheap classifier call, the route read off the plan the Planner made, and an always-information floor.
purpose: Understand what a request asks for before the system answers, acts or writes, in one place.
approach: Give the request, and what the Mind can already see, to an arm that returns one route from the closed list with a reason; an arm that cannot decide raises and the route is never guessed.
out_of_scope: Choosing the worker for each piece (the Planner does that), whether an action is allowed (Judgment Calls) and writing the reply (the Response Writer).
milestones: 1. The route matches a reader's label on the labelled request set (authoritative metric metric-route-a-request).
measures_of_success: The share of requests routed to the route a reader says they ask for.
inputs: A request and, optionally, the view of what the Mind can already see.
outputs: The route (information, act, draft or clarify) and a one sentence reason.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself; the classifier arm makes one model call through Model Plumbing.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("route-a-request", {"request": ...})` returns the route and reason. Until the live stage measures the classifier, the arm the metric selects is the floor, which answers information for everything: a consumer chooses its own arm for itself (the classifier, or `plan_derived` over its own planner's report).
verdict_detail: plan_derived is exactly equal to majority_floor on the metric (plan_derived 0.293 against majority_floor 0.293), so majority_floor stays

name: Response Writer
description: Outputs the plan, the request or the communication the Mind produced, in the form its reader needs and to the quality profile that applies.
purpose: Write what the Mind outputs for its reader.
approach: Write the reply from the results of the delegated pieces to the profile's criteria, saying plainly what a step could not do, and nothing a result did not hold.
out_of_scope: Judging the response against the quality profile (Response Quality does that) and deciding what to say (the Planner and workers do that).
milestones: 1. The written plan, request or communication meets the quality profile that applies (authoritative metric metric-response-writer).
measures_of_success: The written plan, request or communication meets the quality profile that applies.
inputs: The results of the pieces, the reader and the quality profile.
outputs: The written plan, request or communication.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("response-writer", {"results": [], "profile": None})` returns the written text.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: Structure Watch
description: One small call on the best tier, built from a digest made in code, that says where the structure of an intent (its ESOI records) needs attention before more work is built on it, against the recent and planned work. It raises at most three items, often none, and sends each through Judgment Calls: a proposal to a person for what a person wrote, reviewed or owns, what a running experiment holds fixed and anything irreversible, or applied by the AI itself, with the change recorded, for structure the AI made and nobody reviewed.
purpose: Say where the structure needs attention before more work is built on it, with few tokens and without being asked.
approach: Build a capped digest of the changes, recent runs, planned work and the findings of the records' own rules, make one best-tier call only when the digest is new, keep at most three items, leave out what was raised before and is not worse, and route each item through Judgment Calls.
out_of_scope: Watching a run's steps for irreversible or person-owned acts (the Nervous System's consent gate does that), deciding when it runs (Proactivity does that), ordering what it raises (Prioritization does that), and editing records other than as a recorded, undoable change of structure nobody reviewed (ESOI Application does that).
milestones: 1. The planted structural problems are raised and routed, clean structures stay silent, an unchanged digest makes no call and the caps hold (authoritative metric metric-structure-watch).
measures_of_success: Planted problems raised, clean structures silent, no call on an unchanged digest, repeats not raised again unless worse, and the caps held.
parameters: The role structure-watch of the tier table is the only role that runs on the best tier unasked. Input cap 3000 tokens, output cap 500, three items.
inputs: The structure of one intent as tables (solutions, implementations, metrics, experiments, investigations, milestones), the recorded results, the recent runs, review marks (person or ai, by record), the time, and optionally a store of earlier watches, Judgment Calls' decide, ESOI Application's apply and the run's ceilings.
outputs: The items (subject, what, why now, risk, severity, step, route proposal or applied with its recorded change), the items left out as repeats, the tokens and tier used and why a call was or was not made.
effects: Records the watch (time, digest hash, items, tokens, tier, snapshot) in the store it is given; applies a change only to structure marked ai and not held fixed, through ESOI Application.
usage_notes: Justification against siblings: the Nervous System's consent gate reads one step by rule for a risk to do now, a different definition of best (risky steps stopped) from structure that needs attention (planted problems raised, clean ones silent); Proactivity decides when; Metric Upkeep keeps one milestone's metrics measurable and acts; ESOI Application applies a given edit. None looks over the structure for what to attend to first. A run-step risk and a structural risk have different metrics, so this is a solution of its own under the Nervous System.
verdict_detail: best_tier_call leads findings_only (findings_only 0.806 against best_tier_call 1; best guess, not yet significant, two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=0.0625, 5 of 18 cases disagree)

name: Context Retriever
description: Cuts a corpus (files, the text of cards, or the turns of a conversation) into units at natural boundaries and returns, for a request, the units that answer it best first within a token budget, or nothing when the request needs no context. One retrieval for cards, file chunks and memory, measured on one balanced number.
purpose: Pick, from a corpus of files, cards or memory, the pieces of text a task needs within a token budget.
approach: Cut the corpus Internal Context returns into units, rank the units for the request and return the best within a token budget, or nothing when the request needs no context; every arm answers the same call and is scored on one balanced number.
out_of_scope: Formatting the picked text (the renderer where the picks are used does that) and offering what is not asked for (Intuition does that).
milestones: Lexical, latent, dense, fused, reranked, learned and abstaining arms recorded on one number over file, topic, orientation and no-context requests; a model reranker prepared for a recorded cassette.
measures_of_success: The balanced score of metric-context-retriever, which counts the recall of needed files within the budget, graded nDCG, the noise tokens shown, the size of the index, cost and time.
parameters: The budget in tokens, the corpus (a mapping of path to text) and an optional history of past changes; each arm's own settings are constructor arguments.
inputs: A request in words, and the files to retrieve from the first time.
outputs: Hits: unit id, file, first line, score, tokens and text, best first; an empty list means no context is needed.
effects: Reads the corpus it is given and keeps an index and a vector cache in the folder it is given; no network, and no model unless the arm is a model reranker.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("context-retriever", {"query": "where is the retry delay computed?", "files": {"net.py": "def retry_delay(attempt): ..."}})` returns the hits.
verdict_detail: bm25_body is better than abstaining_affinity (two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=8.32e-32, 270 of 395 cases disagree); bm25_body is better than abstaining_aware (two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=5.64e-31, 266 of 395 cases disagree); bm25_body is better than abstaining_fenced (two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=8.32e-32, 270 of 395 cases disagree); bm25_body is better than abstaining_hybrid (two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=5.79e-32, 271 of 395 cases disagree); bm25_body is better than abstaining_learned (two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=3.5e-35, 285 of 395 cases disagree); bm25_body is better than abstaining_recency (two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=5.79e-32, 271 of 395 cases disagree); name: Intuition
description: What comes to mind for a request without being asked for: cards and facts the Subconscious offers because they are close to the request, which the Mind may take or ignore.
purpose: Let useful information surface unasked.
approach: Offer the closest items to a request, within a budget, and let the Mind take or ignore them.
out_of_scope: Answering a query (the Context Retriever does that).
milestones: 1. An offered item is useful often enough that it is kept (metric-the-intuition).
measures_of_success: An offered item is useful often enough that it is kept.
inputs: A request, a limit and, for the arm that learns, a log of what was taken for earlier requests.
outputs: Items offered to the Mind for a request: id, text, score and why it came to mind.
effects: Reads the items Internal Context holds and the log of takes it is given; it writes nothing.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("the-intuition", {"request": "...", "limit": 5})` returns items with id, text, score and why; the Subconscious calls it before the Mind asks. A consumer passes its own log of takes as `history` (request, taken ids, age_days) to the arm that learns from it. In a person's words it is asked for as: show me anything useful I did not ask about, what else should I know, surface related things when I open something, suggestions that come up on their own.
verdict_detail: co_taken is better than nearest_cards (two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=0.00195, 10 of 20 cases disagree)

name: Local File Context
description: Makes the files of a local working folder usable as context for a piece of work: the cards its files need, and the few files to show first with the folders left out. Cards From Files builds the cards; Folder View chooses what the work sees, judging each folder by evidence (its table of markers is a part of Folder View, not a solution of its own).
purpose: Make the files a piece of work sits in available as context, as cards and as the files to show first, without reading what is risky or useless.
approach: Treat a folder of files as one source with two needs: group its files into cards for recall, and choose which files and folders the work sees first, each measured on its own.
out_of_scope: Ranking text for an answer within a token budget from a corpus already read (Context Retriever), keeping cards (Card Store) and reading or writing files in general (Read Files and File Editing).
milestones: 1. Each part reaches its own milestone: the selected builder of Cards From Files and the selected arm of Folder View are the ones their metrics choose (authoritative metric metric-local-file-context, read from the metrics of its two parts).
knowledge: Placement against siblings: Context Retriever picks from material already read and cards already kept, Intuition offers what occurs unasked, Relevant Solutions names ESOI solutions; only these two parts start from a folder of files. Cards From Files and Folder View are separate solutions with their own arms and metrics, so they stay children and are not merged. Folder Judgment (the marker table and its rules, judgment.py and markers.py) has no alternative of its own: all three Folder View arms use it as helper code, so it stays a part of Folder View.
measures_of_success: The metrics of its parts: the balanced score of the card builders and the utility of the folder view.
inputs: A goal, a working folder and a character budget.
outputs: The files to show first with the folders left out (Folder View), and the cards for the folder (Cards From Files).
effects: Reads the folder; writes nothing.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("local-file-context", {"goal": "...", "root": "."})` returns the files to show first and the folders left out; `build` proposes cards. The Subconscious calls it with a working folder.

name: Relevant Solutions
description: Names the consumer's ESOI solutions a request concerns, best first, each with the scopes above it and the solutions that rely on it, so each gets its own consideration.
purpose: Find, for any request, every solution of the consumer's records that deserves its own consideration, so none is skipped.
approach: Rank the records the request matches in the records' own specification index, carry each match to the solution it belongs to or links to, and add each solution's chain of parents and its dependents.
out_of_scope: Forming each solution's prompt and picking its knowledge (the Subconscious composition does that with Cards From Files and Context Retriever), judging the request against a solution (Solution Passes does that) and ranking cards for an answer (Context Retriever does that).
milestones: 1. Recall of the solutions that needed consideration on the hub's relevance cases at the precision floor (metric-relevant-solutions). 2. A cheap model classifier arm measured on a staged sample.
measures_of_success: Every solution that needed its own consideration is named on most cases, with at least a quarter of those named needed.
parameters: limit (solutions before their chains, default 5); depth (levels of the chain, default 3).
inputs: The request, and where the consumer's ESOI records are (a records root the esoi library reads, or an object with the same methods).
outputs: Solutions best first, each with its name, score, the records that reached it, its chain of parents and its dependents.
effects: None; it reads the records only.
usage_notes: Called by the Subconscious composition's prepare step when the consumer passes records. Justification against siblings: Context Retriever picks text units for an answer by a balanced retrieval score, Cards From Files builds cards and Intuition offers what is near; none names the solutions a request concerns, and its definition of best (recall of solutions needing consideration) differs from theirs.
verdict_detail: records_index is better than records_then_model (two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=8.47e-16, 62 of 62 cases disagree)

name: Research Freshness Reader
description: Reads the date each area of the registry was last researched and reports its age against a 90 day bar, naming the stale areas.
purpose: Read the registry's recorded dates and report how old each area's research is.
approach: Read the recorded research dates and report the days since each.
out_of_scope: Deciding which areas to research again (Learning does that) and doing the research.
milestones: 1. The offline stage of metric-research-freshness-reader has a counting result for the arm.
measures_of_success: Every area's research age is read correctly.
parameters: clock: optional, so a test can fix the date.
inputs: An ISO date, or the registry facts together with a consumer's connections.
outputs: Days since the date, or the combined freshness reading with the stale areas named.
effects: None.
usage_notes: The default arm needs nothing from the consumer.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: Model Tier Chooser
description: Picks, for each of the four model tiers (fast, balanced, quality, best), the provider, model and reasoning effort that scores highest on that tier's own metric over public evaluations (cost and speed count for every tier but best), and lets the hub's own measured work per cost override it with enough cases.
purpose: Pick, for each model tier, the model that best fits what the tier is for, by that tier's own metric.
approach: Score each provider, model and effort on the tier's own weighted public evaluations (tier_metrics.csv over registry/tier_public_scores.csv), with cost and speed as factors and an accuracy floor except for best; no number for a required evaluation means not eligible; then let the hub's own passing work per cost override when each arm has enough shared cases (the threshold is data).
out_of_scope: Calling the model (the Vendor Model Caller does that) and the wording of the question (each part does that).
milestones: 1. The offline stage of metric-model-tier-chooser has a counting result for the arm.
measures_of_success: The chosen model per tier is the top of that tier's public metric, with its score breakdown and runner-up, unless the hub's own cases say otherwise.
parameters: bars: optional keyword arguments that set the quality bars.
inputs: tiers (tier name to candidate arms with cases run, cases passed and tokens), prices (rows from the price file), optional credits and defaults.
outputs: A mapping from each tier to the chosen provider, model and effort, with the reason, the stage (public, own or held) and the score breakdown.
effects: None.
usage_notes: The default arm needs nothing from the consumer.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: Vendor Model Caller
description: Plans, answers and lists models for one vendor, or for several through a router that steps to the next model when a provider fails.
purpose: Reach one vendor's model, and step to the next provider when one fails.
approach: Wrap each vendor behind one interface and route each call to the provider that serves its model, with a fallback when it fails.
out_of_scope: Choosing the tier (the Model Tier Chooser does that) and the wording of the question (each part does that).
milestones: Arms for the main vendors and the Claude Code program, a router that fails over, and recorded failover and answer checks.
measures_of_success: A call is answered when the primary provider fails, and a failure that is not the provider's is raised. Vendor answer quality is measured on model-tier-chooser (metric-vendor-answers).
parameters: Per vendor: key, base url, options and fallback models, all constructor arguments; nothing is read from the environment.
inputs: A model id and a prompt, or a planning request.
outputs: Text, a plan or a list of models.
effects: Network calls to the vendor; token totals are kept per calling thread.
usage_notes: The router (multi_provider) is the arm the failover metric selects and the one a consumer wires; the vendor adapters and the keyless claude_cli program are the providers it routes to, recorded as complementary arms of the call_a_model component and never ranked against it. What a subscription call costs counts inside the balanced number of the tier choice, not as a default typed into the selection.
verdict_detail: multi_provider is better than single_provider (two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=7.63e-06, 18 of 30 cases disagree)

name: Agent Action Format
description: Turns what a model wrote as its actions into effects in a folder. The words of an action are a format, and a model does best in the format it was trained on: a provider's native tool calls, an edit format per model family, or a private text protocol. A harness that drives several model families reads each in its own format instead of choosing one by habit.
purpose: Execute a model's actions in the format that model is trained on, so no call is spent on a protocol it must be taught.
approach: Read a reply as the format its model family emits, run each action inside the folder it was given, and return one outcome per action in the order they were written.
out_of_scope: Choosing which model or which loop drives the work (Delegated Agent Sessions does that), running a command safely (Command Execution does that) and editing a single file by instruction (File Editing does that).
milestones: 1. Every scripted reply is executed with its intended effect in each format a model of a supported family emits (authoritative metric metric-agent-action-format).
knowledge: Anthropic documents its bash and text editor tools as client tools whose schema is built into the model, and says models tend to perform better with formats that match their training data (2025-09-11). Aider's own benchmark moved GPT-4 Turbo from 20 to 61 percent by changing only the edit format. A real lane run of the hub loop failed four times in part because the model wrote function-call markup instead of the text protocol, which the parser then ignored. OpenAI apply_patch (V4A) and Gemini CLI tools are researched and not built (registry area agent_action_format).
measures_of_success: Every scripted reply, in every format, leaves the effect it states.
inputs: A model reply and a working folder.
outputs: One outcome per action: its kind, whether it succeeded and its text.
effects: Runs the actions in the working folder; a path outside it is refused.
usage_notes: Call hubofhubs.run("agent-action-format", {"reply": ..., "working_dir": ...}). A paid stage (tasks completed per arm on the same model) is the metric of Delegated Agent Sessions; the native loop of a provider's own agent executes its own calls and cannot be scripted offline.
verdict_detail: any_format is better than native_tool_calls (two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=0.00781, 9 of 15 cases disagree); any_format is better than text_protocol (two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=0.0312, 6 of 15 cases disagree)

name: Command Execution
description: Runs one shell command for an agent in a folder and says what happened: bounded in time and output, refusing the few commands that should not run unattended, and, in the arms that confine, unable to write outside the folder it was given, with a scratch folder that lasts the whole session. Every harness that runs commands needs this, and what holds the boundary (a scan of the command words, or the system) is the choice the metric compares.
purpose: Run an agent's commands in its folder without hanging, flooding its prompt or touching what the person did not hand over.
approach: Run each command in its own process group with a timeout that ends the group, merge and clip its output, refuse the few commands that must never run unattended, and where a sandbox is available let the system enforce the folder boundary.
out_of_scope: Deciding which command to run (the loop that drives the model does that), asking a person before a risky step (Judgment Calls does that) and calling one operation of a connected system (Connected System Operations does that).
milestones: 1. Every scripted case passes: commands run, the floor refuses what it must, a write outside the folder is contained and a scratch folder lasts the session (authoritative metric metric-command-execution).
knowledge: The refusal floor scans a command's words, so a program that opens a path itself passes it (the module text says so); a bubblewrap sandbox enforces the boundary with the disk read-only outside the folder. Anthropic's sandbox runtime (Apache-2.0, beta research preview, filesystem and network restrictions without a container) and Codex CLI's sandbox modes are researched (registry area command_sandbox) and not built. A real lane run lost files between commands until the scratch folder was bound at /tmp for the whole session.
measures_of_success: Every scripted case passes with no model call.
parameters: timeout, environment, scratch and limit, all optional.
inputs: A command and a working folder.
outputs: A result: exit code, merged clipped output, whether it timed out, and the reason it was refused when it was.
effects: Runs the command: it may change files in the working folder (and the scratch folder); a refused command changes nothing.
usage_notes: Call hubofhubs.run("command-execution", {"command": ..., "working_dir": ...}). A harness with its own loop passes the session's scratch folder so files written by one command are there for the next.
verdict_detail: bubblewrap_wrapper leads refusal_floor (refusal_floor 0.818 against bubblewrap_wrapper 1; best guess, not yet significant, two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=0.5, 2 of 11 cases disagree)

name: Connected System Operations
description: Calls an operation of a connected system, such as a write through an MCP server. A consumer that declares its own system's operations (for example a product's operations tool) supplies that as another alternative of the same job.
purpose: Carry out an operation of a connected system on the AI's behalf.
approach: Call one write operation of a connected system through its protocol, with the operation named by the goal, and report the result; nothing else is changed.
out_of_scope: Deciding to call it (the Planner and Delegation do that), the system's enduring integrations (Hands does that) and editing files (File Editing does that).
milestones: 1. A called operation does what was asked and nothing else (authoritative metric metric-connected-system-operations).
measures_of_success: A called operation does what was asked and nothing else.
parameters: model, max_turns, run_id and context_preamble, all optional; the writer the arm may use is a constructor argument.
inputs: An operation and its arguments.
outputs: The result of the operation, or the reason it was declined.
effects: Changes files or calls a write operation inside the writer the consumer grants; nothing changes when the arm declines.
usage_notes: Call hubofhubs.run('connected-system-operations', {'goal': ..., 'brief': ...}); the model or writer the arm needs is a constructor argument the consumer provides.

name: Delegated Agent Sessions
description: Hands open-ended work to an agent that runs in its own session and reports back. An arm is an agent harness, the model provider it drives and a tier: Claude Code (one shot, steerable, ACP) drives Anthropic models, Codex CLI drives OpenAI models, and opencode drives any provider it holds a key for. Two arms need no Claude Code: opencode inside the hub's shared wrapper (the hub's frame as its instructions, the shared ceilings, the code check with the stop decision, an outside-folder report), and the hub's own loop speaking the provider's native tool calling (Anthropic tool use measured; Gemini and OpenAI written but unmeasured). A consumer declares the providers it holds credentials for and gets the best measured arm among the ones it can run.
purpose: Get open-ended work done by an agent in its own session.
approach: Hand the goal to an agent that runs in its own session under a written done-standard and a turn limit, and return what it reported and whether it met the goal.
out_of_scope: Editing a single file (File Editing does that), calling one operation (Connected System Operations does that) and deciding the pieces (the Planner does that).
milestones: 1. A coding goal counts as done only when its own written tests pass after the arm has run, with the tests restored by the harness (authoritative metric metric-delegated-agent-sessions).
knowledge: A harness has parts that are not whole harnesses. Command execution and the action format are their own solutions (siblings in Tools). Folded here as arm features and metric stages, with the reason: working memory within a run (the hub loop's STATE block, the native session's task tools) and the cost basis (plain input plus output tokens and the CLI's own dollars, one basis for every arm) have no competing alternatives that stand alone; session persistence, resume, stop and steer belong to the session experience contract and the arms that implement it; approval of a risky step belongs to Judgment Calls; verification of a result belongs to Goal Completion and the hub's code check of written text, which the native arm uses after its session; which loop to start on is a cascade of arms, recorded as a specified alternative. Measured 2026-11-10 on the same model: see the changelog.
measures_of_success: A general task that is not coding counts as done only when the agent's final report holds every expected fact, the run says it met the goal and the files are unchanged.
parameters: model, max_turns, run_id and context_preamble, all optional; provider and tier (the arm) and the writer are constructor arguments.
inputs: A goal, a brief and its done-standard.
outputs: A result that says whether the goal was met, with the reason.
effects: Changes files or calls a write operation inside the writer the consumer grants; nothing changes when the arm declines.
usage_notes: Call hubofhubs.run('delegated-agent-sessions', {'goal': ..., 'brief': ...}); the model or writer the arm needs is a constructor argument the consumer provides. To pick the arm for a consumer, call choose_agent_arm(providers) from hubofhubs.api with the providers it holds credentials for (anthropic, openai, gemini, deepseek); it returns the best eligible arm at the latest cascade stage reached, else the best eligible arm by public prior or idea rating, with the reason.
verdict_detail: beaten by opencode_hub_runner@provider=anthropic,tier=fast, opencode_runner@provider=anthropic,tier=fast: native_tool_loop_runner@provider=anthropic,tier=fast leads native_tool_calling_loop_runner@provider=anthropic,tier=fast (native_tool_calling_loop_runner@provider=anthropic,tier=fast 0.682 against native_tool_loop_runner@provider=anthropic,tier=fast 0.893; best guess, not yet significant, two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=1, 9 of 9 cases disagree); best guess, not yet significant: opencode_hub_runner@provider=anthropic,tier=fast leads native_tool_loop_runner@provider=anthropic,tier=fast (opencode_hub_runner@provider=anthropic,tier=fast 0.893 against native_tool_loop_runner@provider=anthropic,tier=fast 0.893; two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=1, 9 of 9 cases disagree); more cases would settle it; best guess, not yet significant: opencode_runner@provider=anthropic,tier=fast leads native_tool_loop_runner@provider=anthropic,tier=fast (opencode_runner@provider=anthropic,tier=fast 0.893 against native_tool_loop_runner@provider=anthropic,tier=fast 0.893; two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=0.195, 9 of 9 cases disagree); more cases would settle it; native_tool_loop_runner@provider=anthropic,tier=fast leads solution_loop_runner@provider=anthropic,tier=fast (solution_loop_runner@provider=anthropic,tier=fast 0.787 against native_tool_loop_runner@provider=anthropic,tier=fast 0.893; best guess, not yet significant, two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=1, 9 of 9 cases disagree); stream_json_goal_runner@provider=anthropic,tier=fast is exactly equal to native_tool_loop_runner@provider=anthropic,tier=fast on the metric (stream_json_goal_runner@provider=anthropic,tier=fast 0.893 against native_tool_loop_runner@provider=anthropic,tier=fast 0.893), so native_tool_loop_runner@provider=anthropic,tier=fast stays

name: File Editing
description: Changes a file by instruction and reports what changed. The alternatives do the same job at the same level: a one-call model edit and, as researched candidates with no arm yet, exact string replacement and patch formats.
purpose: Make the file change that was asked for, and no other.
approach: Land one bounded change to a file named by the goal in one model call, with the file read first and the change checked against it; nothing else is changed.
out_of_scope: Deciding what to change (the Planner does that), checking the goal (Goal Completion does that) and running open-ended agent work (Delegated Agent Sessions does that).
milestones: 1. A coding goal counts as done only when its own written tests pass after the arm has run, with the tests restored by the harness (authoritative metric metric-file-editing).
measures_of_success: A coding goal counts as done only when its own written tests pass after the arm has run, with the tests restored by the harness.
parameters: model, max_turns, run_id and context_preamble, all optional; the writer the arm may use is a constructor argument.
inputs: A file instruction and a folder it may write in.
outputs: A report of the file change, or the reason it was declined; nothing changes when it declines.
effects: Changes files or calls a write operation inside the writer the consumer grants; nothing changes when the arm declines.
usage_notes: Call hubofhubs.run('file-editing', {'goal': ..., 'brief': ...}); the model or writer the arm needs is a constructor argument the consumer provides. No consumer in this ecosystem wires a file writer today; retiring this solution is proposed.
verdict_detail: best guess, not yet significant: none 0.298 against fast_edit 0.972 on the point estimate; no case counts or per-case rows allow a test

name: File Reading
description: Lists and reads the text files of a folder, never outside it: the world-facing half of working with files that Cards From Files builds on.
purpose: Read the files a task or a card builder needs, without leaving the folder it was given.
approach: List the text files of one folder and read the ones asked for, never outside the folder and never more than a size cap, so one read cannot flood a context.
out_of_scope: Writing files (File Editing does that) and deciding which files matter (Cards From Files and the Context Retriever do that).
milestones: 1. Read the files a task or a card builder needs, without leaving the folder it was given. (authoritative metric metric-read-files).
measures_of_success: Read the files a task or a card builder needs, without leaving the folder it was given.
inputs: A folder, optionally paths and suffixes.
outputs: The file paths of a folder, and the text of the files asked for.
effects: Reads the folder; writes nothing.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("read-files", {"root": ".", "paths": []})` reads the text files of a folder.

name: Web Search
description: One narrow call: a query in, a response of hits out. The hub ships thin adapters over open-source and hosted search services, and a consumer may provide its own.
purpose: Run one web search and return its hits with their sources.
approach: Send the query to the chosen service and return hits with a title, a link and a snippet.
out_of_scope: Public research papers (Science does that) and reading a person's own data (Internal Context declares where it is and File Reading reads it).
milestones: 1. The offline stage of metric-web-search has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 2. The live stage of metric-web-search has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 3. The selected arm is the one the cascade of metric-web-search chooses (rule S33).
measures_of_success: Result rows with a title, a link and a snippet for a query.
parameters: The service address or API key of the chosen arm, a timeout and an optional daily limit.
inputs: A query, a result limit and an optional instruction for a model-backed arm.
outputs: A response of hits (title, link, snippet, date, passages and their kind), an optional direct answer and the queries issued; raises SearchBackendError on failure.
effects: One network request per search to the chosen service, counted against the daily limit when one is set.
usage_notes: The hub ships arms (searxng, serper, brave, tavily, gemini, provider) and a selector over them (hubofhubs.the_world.tools.web_search.backends.select_search_backend). None is selected by default: no metric run exists yet, so a consumer names an arm in its selections or provides its own object.
verdict_detail: gemini is better than provider (two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=1.1e-05, 22 of 40 cases disagree)

name: Cards From Files
description: Proposes a proportionate, current set of cards for material a consumer already keeps in files, without writing them.
purpose: Propose the cards a folder of files needs, in the card store record shape, for the Subconscious to keep and recall.
approach: Group the files that belong together, describe each group, and report which cards an edit has made stale.
out_of_scope: Keeping the cards (Card Store does that) and reading or writing files in general (Read Files and File Editing do that).
milestones: 1. The selected builder's balanced score on the mixed pinned cases is at least that of every free topic builder, with a store far below one card per file (metric-cards-from-files).
measures_of_success: The files a piece of work needed are inside the first cards the fixed selector picks, with little noise and with files of more than one folder bundled when the task spans them, from a store of at most 0.25 cards per file, at a price per build a team would pay.
parameters: The model provider, for a builder that calls one.
inputs: A folder root, the list of files to read, and the cards already kept for it.
outputs: Cards in the card-store record shape (grouping, summary, keywords, files with their hashes), and the ids of kept cards whose files changed.
effects: Reads files; writes nothing (the caller writes through card-store).
usage_notes: Run it for a first index and after edits, passing the cards already kept so a builder skips covered files. The per-file builder is the free floor; a builder that calls a model has to buy its price in accuracy on the balanced score. The per-file builder is a baseline for finding one file, not a card builder. The free topic builders (cochange_topic_cards, import_graph_topic_cards, the replay of the saved paid build) are scored for free; docs/how-to/iterate-on-card-builders-without-repeating-model-calls.md says how to iterate before any paid run.

name: Folder View
description: Chooses, for a piece of work in a working folder, the few files to show before it starts and the folders to leave out, judging each folder by evidence in it (a project file beside it, a marker inside it, what its files are) so dependency, build, cache, generated and risky places are never scanned, and reports what it left out and why. Part of Local File Context. Its folder judgment (a table of markers and rules, judgment.py and markers.py) is helper code shared by every arm, with no alternative of its own, so it is a part of this solution and not a solution.
purpose: Choose the files of a working folder a piece of work should be shown first, and never read what is risky or unlikely to help, for any programming language and tool.
approach: Judge each folder by evidence and a table of markers, leave out what is dependency, build, cache, generated, binary or risky and say why, then rank the rest by what the work itself points at; every arm answers the same call and is scored on one number.
out_of_scope: Ranking pieces of text for an answer within a token budget from a corpus already read (Context Retriever does that), building cards from the files (Cards From Files does that), offering what was not asked for (Intuition does that), naming the consumer's ESOI solutions a request concerns (Relevant Solutions does that), and reading or editing the files (Read Files and File Editing do that).
milestones: 1. The selected arm's utility on the small and corpus cases is above the ported baseline's, with no pick in a risky folder (metric-folder-view). 2. A model arm is measured against the best free arm on the same cases and kept only if it buys its price in utility.
measures_of_success: The files a worker needs are among the first shown within the budget, nothing from a dependency, build, cache or risky folder is shown unasked, and every folder left out is listed with its reason.
parameters: The goal text, the context text, the folder, a character budget, the trail of files earlier runs used (optional) and a cap on the files scanned.
inputs: A goal, a context, a working folder and a budget in characters.
outputs: Picks best first (relative path, reason, size; named when the goal names it; flagged when it names a file inside a risky folder), the folders and risky files left out with the reason of each, and counts of the files passed over one by one.
effects: Reads the folder (names, sizes and the first 2 KB of each file); writes nothing and calls no model unless the arm is a model arm.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("folder-view", {"goal": "...", "context": "", "root": ".", "budget_chars": 24000})` returns the choice. The hub's own work harness calls it before its first model call and lists the folders left out in its folder map. Justification against siblings: Context Retriever returns text units of a corpus that is already read and indexed, by a token-budget retrieval score, and its folder-level cost is the index; this solution decides which folders of a live working folder may be scanned at all and which files to show, never reads a risky place, and its definition of best adds safety and the report of what was left out. Cards From Files proposes cards for kept files, Intuition offers what is near a request, and Relevant Solutions names ESOI solutions; none chooses files of a folder for a piece of work or judges folders. One new use of Context Retriever was considered first and rejected: its input is a mapping of path to text, so a corpus of thousands of files, dependency folders and secrets would have to be read before it could be judged.
verdict_detail: best guess, not yet significant: model_pick 0.97 against evidence_ranked 0.97 on the point estimate; no case counts or per-case rows allow a test; evidence_ranked is better than ported_baseline (two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=1.94e-06, 36 of 41 cases disagree)
